Good question.
If 2/3 instances fails but one succeeds, we have a result like:

> Instance '2894947af0addff6805fed312a9d6d109bd7813d6d0d6b9e64ec5bb1e8c20f98': Command accepted. Starting execution.
Instance '23b9f272afebff4a0d5132b28b6805106c1b5cea5cce36a877b0404018e59161': An error occurred while executing the command. If the issue persists, verify your command syntax and ensure any specified working directory is an absolute path to an accessible directory.
Instance 'a6d0e79727a1d9d853d32e2fffab8b760507fa6d8471512eb7401ee836e8a73a': An error occurred while executing the command. If the issue persists, verify your command syntax and ensure any specified working directory is an absolute path to an accessible directory.
Command request was not accepted on 2 of 3 instance(s). See the messages above for details.

But yes we don't return a result to print a pretty json at the end. This is intentional. We need the command ro raise AzureResponseError to produce a non-zero exit code. Printing success-shaped JSON before raising could be confusing for customers and automation. When all instances accept the request, the structured JSON is returned normally.

Good catch. The no-retry branch was meant to mean "polling verified the assertion," but when `_should_retry_for_provisioning_state` returns `(False, None)` we never polled. Fixed in 6cc8f0e6a3: `_cmd_with_retry` now calls `result.assert_with_checks(provisioning_checks)` in that branch so the assertion fails loudly instead of being silently dropped.

Added two regression tests in `test_aks_provisioning_retry.py`:

- `test_missing_provisioning_state_fails_loudly` — body with `id` but no `provisioningState` now raises `JMESPathCheckAssertionError`.
- `test_missing_id_fails_loudly` — body with `provisioningState` but no `id` now raises `JMESPathCheckAssertionError`.

An audit of `test_aks_commands.py` confirmed no existing AKS test relies on the silent-pass branch (every adapter-intercepted check is against a command that returns `provisioningState` at the top level), so the behaviour change is safe for the current test corpus.
